verdict: ULAM'S METHOD APPLIED TO PERTURBATION SPREAD, AND IT DOES NOT WORK HERE. Two claims this module originally made are WITHDRAWN, both refuted by checks that cost minutes. FIRST, the response-size distribution was offered as evidence for branching -- heavy tail, Fano 91.3, log-log slope -1.41 against critical Galton-Watson's -1.5, 689/1400 exact zeros. Permuting each knockout's z-scores WITHIN its own non-tide columns leaves the count above threshold unchanged by construction, and measured, all seven statistics are BIT-IDENTICAL under that permutation. They are functions of the per-knockout marginal and carry ZERO bits about topology. A heavy tail is consistent with branching and equally consistent with anything else that makes heavy-tailed responses. SECOND, Monte Carlo was justified on the grounds that two-terminal reliability is #P-complete. It is -- in general, and not here: at depth 2 the direct edge and each 2-path through a common neighbour are EDGE-DISJOINT, hence independent, so P(reach) = 1 - (1-p_st) * prod_x (1 - p_sx p_xt) exactly, and at depth 3 the correction is both tiny and monotone, so it cannot reorder. There was never a quantity here without a closed form. WHAT SURVIVES IS THE CROSS-SECTION, because it contrasts partners against non-partners and the permutation destroys it: P(PPI partner moves | gene knocked out) = 0.00941 against 0.00150, 6.26x. That is measured against a FLAT background, and against a degree- and move-frequency-matched background the enrichment is much smaller; the flat number should not be quoted alone. R0 IS A RANGE AND NOT A NUMBER: the naive p*<k> gives 0.25, the excess-degree formula 0.72 (p/p_c = 0.72), and both assume a locally tree-like graph that this one is not -- PPI clustering is ~0.20 against ~0.002 for a degree-matched random graph, so the configuration-model figure is an upper bound of unknown tightness. Estimators span roughly 0.56 to 1.25, which straddles 1, so THE SUB- VERSUS SUPERCRITICAL QUESTION IS NOT ANSWERABLE FROM THIS DATA and the earlier flat assertion of 'subcritical' overstated it. MONTE CARLO IS NOT USABLE AT PER-GENE RESOLUTION HERE, AND THIS WAS TESTED FIRST, BEFORE ANY PERFORMANCE NUMBER. Two independent runs at 3000 replicates agree with each other at Spearman 0.276 -- the estimator does not reproduce ITSELF -- while agreeing with the cheap linear walk at 0.419. So the MC-vs-linear disagreement is sampling noise, not nonlinearity. The arithmetic is elementary: at R0 = 0.72 the reachability probabilities are ~1e-4, so at 3000 replicates most genes are hit zero or one times and the ranking is Poisson noise. THIS IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE FROM THE PREVIOUS TWO Monte Carlos in this repo, which were rank-decorative; this one is statistically infeasible, and the distinction matters because it says WHERE MC can still work. SO THE MC IS SPENT WHERE ULAM SPENT IT: ON THE AGGREGATE. He never computed the probability that a particular neutron reached a particular place; he computed the multiplication factor. An aggregate over ~10^4 genes has a relative standard error smaller by sqrt(n). The aggregate here is the BLAST RADIUS, the number of genes a knockout moves, which is the direct neutron-count analogue and is measured and held out. Baseline ladder, Spearman against the true count over all 1400 knockouts in 5-fold CV: train mean -0.0401, PPI degree alone 0.3135, essentiality alone 0.4286, a GBM on node features 0.4325, the analytic mean-field cascade alone 0.3171, node-GBM plus the cascade 0.4120 (-0.0204 over the GBM without it), and adding the MC moments 0.3957 (-0.0163). THE CASCADE FEATURE DOES NOT BEAT THE NODE FEATURES IT IS BUILT FROM. A branching simulation that cannot beat degree-plus-essentiality in a GBM has demonstrated nothing beyond restating degree, and that is the honest reading of -0.0204. AND THE MC MOMENTS ADD -0.0163 ON TOP -- a LOSS, so sampling does not pay for itself here either. The cascade SD tracks the cascade mean at +0.975 and P(zero) at -0.922; those are not quite the perfect monotonicity that would make them the mean in disguise, but near-monotone features that cost a 600-replicate simulation and then REDUCE held-out accuracy are not a finding to defend on a technicality. This is the third Monte Carlo in this repo to fail to earn its cost, and the three failed differently: the first two were rank-decorative, this one is unaffordable at per-gene resolution and unhelpful at aggregate resolution. WHAT THIS CANNOT SAY. Only 674 of 15,183 specific movers (4.4%) are direct PPI partners of the knocked-out gene, so a cascade on this graph could never have explained WHICH genes move -- it was only ever testable on HOW MANY, which is why blast radius is the target. The cross-section is measured at hop 1, from a gene that was destroyed, and then applied at hops 2-3 where the source is merely perturbed; that is the same assumption Ulam made in reusing one cross-section at every collision, but it is far less safe here, and it would bias R0 upward. CRISPRi knockdown is partial (median 42.8% transcript remaining), so 'knocked out' is itself an idealisation. Evaluation is all 1400 knockouts, deliberately NOT the 378 scorable ones, because filtering on >=5 movers would condition the evaluation set on the target being predicted.
